description: Join UCSF researchers for a practical look at new generative AI models, tools, platforms and workflows designed to facilitate and expedite scientific research! Title: "Benchmarking Automated Scientific Enquiry: When AI co-scientists outpace peer review, what becomes the arbiter of truth?" Featured Speaker: Luca Foschini, PhD President & CEO, Sage Bionetworks Seminar 3-4pm, Networking Reception 4-5pm Share the Flyer! Bio: Luca Foschini, PhD, is President and CEO of Sage Bionetworks, a nonprofit that builds open infrastructure for biomedical data sharing, including the Synapse platform and community challenges such as DREAM. Before Sage he co-founded Evidation Health, where as Chief Data Scientist he spent over a decade leading research on wearable and real-world data for health. He holds a PhD in Computer Science from UC Santa Barbara, has published more than 70 peer-reviewed papers, and in a previous life represented Italy at the International Olympiad in Informatics. Abstract: In under two years, AI systems went from grade-school math to research-level problems, and the length of tasks an agent can complete reliably keeps doubling every few months. More than twenty AI co-scientists now promise to search the literature, generate hypotheses, analyze data and write up results. Do they reason like scientists? Recent evidence says not yet: agents often gather evidence and then ignore it, and better scaffolds barely help. The deeper problem is verification. AI moves fastest where answers can be checked instantly, as in code or proofs, while biology checks its claims at the pace of the wet lab and of peer review. I will walk through what works today, where these tools fail, and how benchmarks run as living community efforts, kept fresh and re-run on every new model, can keep us honest about what is still true. If you can't make it in person, join us via webinar: https://ucsf.zoom.us/j/91612960363?pwd=G4UDfMm6Zucceb5OIfd0gXohGBcfpK.1, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform

description: This course, UCSF’s most comprehensive continuing education course in primary care, will present an extensive review of new developments in outpatient medicine, controversies in primary care practice, and updates from diverse clinical specialties that impact primary care. The course will focus on the skills and strategies needed in day-to-day office practice. The curriculum will feature in-depth discussion of challenging cases in preventive medicine, common problems in ambulatory care, and a broad selection of acute and chronic illnesses. The course will utilize formal lectures, case discussions, an audience response system, questions and answers, and a detailed syllabus. Ample time will be reserved for interprofessional discussion of challenging cases. The course is presented by the UCSF Division of General Internal Medicine of the Department of Medicine and is sponsored by the Office of Continuing Medical Education, University of California, San Francisco. Participate in person at the Marines' Memorial Hotel in San Francisco or tune in virtually for this 3 day conference. Included in your registration fee is access to the course recordings on demand after the conference and for 30 days after the course.

description: California Welfare and Institutions Code Psychiatric Holds (5150): What to Know and How to Do It Right Dominic Tarpey, LCSW Senior Quality Analyst UCSF Langley Porter Psychiatric Hospital Learning objectives: At the end of this presentation, attendees will: Understand the history, intent, and scope of the California Welfare and Institutions Code pertaining to involuntary commitmentUnderstand the criteria and parameters by which a person can be involuntarily detainedUnderstand the rights a person who has been placed in an involuntary hold retain, and the rights for due process---------- This training session is only for UCSF Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences clinical faculty, staff, trainees, and other mental health clinicians at UCSF Health hospitals, clinics, and programs. If you provide direct patient care at Langley Porter Psychiatric Hospital, the Nancy Friend Pritzker Psychiatry Building, or any UCSF Health location in San Francisco and are new to the department, have not yet been certified, or your certification is expiring soon, then please attend one of these trainings. Please note that this training is required for faculty, clinical staff, and trainees—including physicians, psychologists, nurse practitioners, and masters-level therapists (e.g. LCSW, LMFT, MSW, MFT). Please consult your supervisor if you have any questions about whether you are required to attend. Trainees should consult with RTP or their fellowship coordinator. Continuing education credits are not available for these trainings. Other clinical staff—such as RNs, LVNs, expressive arts therapists, BCBAs, medical assistants—are not required to do this training. However, any staff are welcome to attend as an educational opportunity. Please coordinate with your supervisor if you wish to attend. Additional information: San Francisco CBHS wallet cards are issued for authorized clinicians (there are no certificates).Continuing education credit is not available.This training is offered periodically during the year, usually quarterly.

description: Please join us for a special CTB/OFS seminar with Dr. Laertis Ikonomou, University at Buffalo School of Dental Medicine, on Friday, October 23, 2026, from 10:00 - 11:00 am. Friday, October 23rd, 10:00 - 11:00 am, HSW-302 Presentation Title: "Deciphering Gene Regulatory Networks in Early Lung Epithelium" Dr. Laertis Ikonomou is an Associate Professor at the Department of Oral Biology, University at Buffalo. His major research interests are in the areas of pluripotent stem cell biology and developmental biology, with emphasis on foregut and dental in vivo biology and its applications in directed differentiation of pluripotent stem cells. His research, supported by the NIH and the American Thoracic Society, defined for the first time the genetic program of lung primordial progenitors and current studies are focused on the gene regulatory networks underlying early lung epithelial fate decisions. description: Join Us Friday, October 23, 2026 "Sight and Sound as Deep Phenotypes: Audiovisual AI for Precision Medicine" Speaker: Benjamin Glicksberg, PhD Associate Professor and Chief of Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Artificial Intelligence and Human Health Department, Icahn School of Medicine, Mount Sinai 10:30-11:00 am coffee/refreshments / Seminar at 11am-12pm. Flyer Benjamin Glicksberg, Ph.D. is an Associate Professor and the Chief of Entrepreneurship and Innovation for the Windreich Department of Artificial Intelligence and Human Health at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. He is the Founding Director of the Center for AI in Children’s Health and is the Director of the Digital Discovery Program within the Hasso Plattner Institute for Digital Health. Formerly, he served on the leadership team as the VP and Head of Data Science and Machine Learning of Character Biosciences, a precision health drug development company using genomics to develop novel therapeutics for progressive diseases of aging. Dr. Glicksberg co-founded ArtemisAI Labs, which delivers real-time, objective health assessments at the bedside using audiovisual monitoring, focusing primarily on neonatal care. Dr. Glicksberg received his Ph.D. from the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and proudly completed post-doctoral work with Atul Butte, MD PhD at the University of California, San Francisco. description: What helps people feel that they truly belong—and what happens when they do? Join the UCSF Climate and Belonging's Fostering Awareness Speaker Series on October 28th from 12:10–1:00 p.m. for The Science of Belonging, featuring UCSF’s Mica Estrada, PhD. Part of the Fostering Awareness: Dimensions of Belonging series, this session will explore the research behind belonging and the ways our environments, relationships, and everyday interactions can influence whether people feel valued, connected, and able to thrive. Dr. Estrada is Associate Dean of Opportunity & Engagement and Professor in the UCSF School of Nursing. Her research examines social influence, identity, values, kindness, well-being, mentorship, and approaches that strengthen inclusion and persistence in STEMM communities.
